status: PROPOSED - needs one visual A/B against hero assets before any re-assignment
supersedes: specs/materials/toon_preset_stack.v1.json (withdrawn - it proposed a parallel MI mechanism)
principle: ONE look mechanism, already in the project: the ToonProfile. The masters are Substrate Toon (MaterialExpressionSubstrateToonBSDF_*) and each master holds a ToonProfile reference, so the look is DATA and one profile edit re-looks everything that inherits it. No new masters, no parallel preset instances, no second palette.

where_the_look_actually_lives.content: the Material Function vocabulary (grade / style / functional) + the Substrate Toon BSDF
Melusina_RoseGold, R1999_Gold, R1999_Ivory, Melusina_InkNavy, BeatPulse, ShadowDreamBias, RimWarmth, PaletteTint
colour, texture set, tiling, per-asset hue nudge - and nothing else

canon_profile_set.role: the hero / world default (already assigned to M_Master_Toon_Universal)

canon_values.DiffuseRamp: warm-violet #352D40 family warmth + melancholic depth (as authored)
canon_values.ShadowExtinctionCoefficient: tune so shadows read PLUM, never black

canon_profile_set.role: Poitou limestone, the abbey, the lanes
crystal, chime glass, the focal gem

retire_from_assignment.why: they are 15 redirects into the third-party _304FilmSpine pack, and they are where the 'shadow dream' look comes from. KEEP the assets (the Musical Dream biome family and the author_musical_dream_mis.py output still point through them); just stop assigning them to the canon masters.
not_retired: MF_NikkiDreamGrade stays the single grade function - re-preset, do not rip out
MF_Impressionist_Impasto stays available for a painterly tier
MF_Madoka / MF_Itto are the other stylistic families - stop inheriting them

palette_canon.retire: MPC_Portfolio_Palette (second authority, written by a one-off script)

changes.why: it is the literal 'shadow dream' and it is not consumed by the toon master today
the identity canon; plum shadows are a genre convention, not a hack (OSS toon references do the same)
the identity canon's lilac; lilac is currently missing from the palette entirely

do_not: let an MI override a palette-driven value
let an instance override Cymatic_BeatPulse / Cymatic_EmissiveScale - MPC_Cymatics_Driver owns those

gate.extend: Content/Python/check_toon_profile.py (the project already has this tool - do not create a parallel one)
checks: no canon master resolves to a _304FilmSpine profile
no MI overrides a palette-driven parameter
exactly one palette MPC is written by C++

rollout: 1. the owner edits ONE profile (TP_Melusina) and the three MPC values, then looks at 3-4 hero assets
2. re-point the few materials that actually need a different tier onto the canon profile set
3. re-parent nothing; most assets inherit the master profile already
4. wire the gate into the convergence checklist
